solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Greek philosopher's very constant values

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
c is the standard symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to rate something is to value it, so rates means values

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker's principles are described as very constant.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition ends with 's: the answer plus 'is' reads as Socrates's very constant values, so the wordplay sits after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian thinker of the fifth century BC, a leading figure in Greek philosophy.

clue.text: One providing crude painting easily

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oils
well can mean easily, as in 'it could well happen'

explanation.surface: Someone producing a rough, unpolished picture without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: Crude looks like an adjective describing the painting, but here it is crude oil, the unrefined petroleum.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a borehole that yields crude petroleum, so it is the thing providing crude.

clue.text: Soup dish served up in one marketplace

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upward, so the letters read from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundary

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one and the start of marketplace

explanation.surface: A bowl of soup being dished out at a market stall.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup, served as a dish in its broth.

clue.text: Lid of pan turned upside down

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something upside down puts its last letter at the top

parts.note: a pot is a cooking pan

explanation.surface: A saucepan lid flipped over on the hob.
explanation.definitionFit: A top is a cover or cap for a container, the same thing as a lid.

clue.text: Firm dates arranged quickly

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be reordered
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: Appointments that were fixed in a hurry and are now set.
explanation.walkthrough: Firm looks like a business, but it is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadfast means resolute and unwavering, which is the adjective sense of firm.

clue.text: Frittered money with some terrible wine

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow, so a portion of them is taken

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of terrible and the start of wine

explanation.surface: Someone wasted their cash on dreadful plonk.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow money is an idiom for spending it wastefully, so the past tense is a match for squandered.

clue.text: Airline owns around a thousand islands in the Caribbean

indicators.note: around says one word wraps itself about the next pieces

parts.note: BA is British Airways
to own something is to have it
taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An airline holds about a thousand Caribbean islands, a joke on how many routes it flies.
explanation.walkthrough: Around looks like 'approximately' in the surface, but it tells one word to wrap the next pieces; the Bahamas are strictly in the Atlantic but are usually counted as Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bahamas is an island nation in the Atlantic, usually grouped with the Caribbean, made up of hundreds of islands.

clue.text: Blunder and fear losing face

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so losing it drops the opening letter

parts.note: terror is great fear

explanation.surface: Someone makes a mistake and is afraid of being humiliated.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, which is what a blunder is.

clue.text: Fruit precisely gathered

indicators.note: gathered here means understood from what was heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: plumb means exactly, as in plumb in the middle

explanation.surface: Fruit picked with great care.
explanation.walkthrough: Gathered looks like harvesting the fruit, but it means heard; the B of plumb is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum is a stone fruit, so it is a straight example of fruit.

clue.text: Edited chapter includes one diagram

indicators.note: includes says the reworked letters hold another piece within them
an edited text has been reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be reordered
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A revised book chapter now contains a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie chart is a circular graphic split into slices, a kind of diagram.

clue.text: Adolescent support of course to bother journalist

parts.note: a tee is the peg supporting a golf ball on the course
to nag is to pester or bother
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A teenager is naturally inclined to pester a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' reads as 'naturally', but it means of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenaged describes someone in their teens, the same age span as adolescent.

clue.text: Animal in young herd, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A creature that might be found among a group of young cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A greyhound is a breed of racing dog, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Horse and sheep heading west, then east

indicators.note: in an across entry, heading west means travelling right to left, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A horse and a sheep travel west, then turn east.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare is a female horse.

clue.text: A large tree growing on mountaintops

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
a pine is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: A big tree flourishing high up on the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine plants grow in high mountain areas above the tree line, so the adjective fits things growing on mountaintops.

clue.text: Forthcoming, as shop assistants may be?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: about to happen, as in what lies ahead
second meaning: located inside a shop, where staff work

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal sense of the phrase; forthcoming also looks as if it means chatty, which shop assistants might be.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in store is coming up in the future, and staff working in a shop are literally inside the store.

clue.text: Judge stupid people scornfully at first

parts.note: asses are fools

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of scornfully

explanation.surface: A judge sneers at foolish people from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Judge looks like a noun for the person, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to evaluate or form an opinion on, the verb sense of judge.

clue.text: Singer contributing to lyrics in a track

indicators.note: the answer gives part of its letters to the run of words that follows, so it sits inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of lyrics through in and a to the start of track

explanation.surface: A vocalist helping write the words of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was the famous American crooner, an example of a singer.

clue.text: Experts at chess regularly lost?

indicators.note: letters lost at regular intervals leaves every other one, beginning with the first

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters are kept

explanation.surface: Wondering whether chess masters keep losing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aces are people who excel at something, which is what experts are.

clue.text: Small bear starts to eat some solids

parts.note: a cub is a young bear

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, taken from the words that follow

parts.note: the opening letters of eat and some

explanation.surface: A little bear begins eating some solid food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubes are three-dimensional geometric shapes with six square faces, a kind of solid.

clue.text: That's unusually also something seen in a cloakroom

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd way, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be reordered
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Remarking on something odd that turns up in a coat room.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is a tall pole with hooks for hats and coats, typical furniture in a cloakroom.

clue.text: Root — one going underground?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a swollen underground stem or root, like a potato
second meaning: a joke word for someone who rides London's Tube trains

explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground; the question mark flags the invented word for a passenger on it. Both senses point below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuber is a thick fleshy underground part of a plant, close enough to a root, and one who travels by Tube is jokingly a commuter of that kind.

clue.text: Sailor's old instrument is perfect

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, and the 's adds S
O is the abbreviation for old
a lute is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A seaman's antique instrument is in flawless condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and total, as in absolute bliss, which is one sense of perfect.

clue.text: Go back home, finally, with two books

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the closing letter of home
B is the abbreviation for book, given twice

explanation.surface: Heading home at last, carrying a couple of books.
explanation.definitionFit: To ebb is to recede, as the tide does, which is to go back.

clue.text: Crazy attempt backfiring

indicators.note: something backfiring turns back on itself, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: a stab is an attempt, as in have a stab at it

explanation.surface: A mad try that goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats is informal for mad, from having bats in the belfry.

clue.text: Man perhaps requiring lip salve frequently

indicators.note: frequently means at many regular points, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A man who keeps needing lip balm.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is not a person but the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of an isle.

clue.text: Pet perhaps named Rob, weirdly

indicators.note: weirdly means in a strange way, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A pet that might oddly have been called Rob.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dobermann is a breed of dog often kept as a pet or guard dog, so it is an example of a pet.
